subject: GreenGrid latency spike — mitigation & customer comms
messages:
From: connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, maya_srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] GreenGrid prod latency spike (us-east-1)

Laura —

Monitoring picked up a sustained latency spike for GreenGrid (account RG-3472) starting ~09:05 PDT. P50/P95/P99 all elevated; 4x increase at P95. Errors are low (no large error budget burn) but token latency and request queuing are visible across the serving layer. This is affecting their API-backed inference calls (region us-east-1).

What we've seen so far: 
- Spike correlated with a model variant rollout (gptx-13b-q4) at 08:58 PDT.
- KV cache miss rate jumped; some large KV evictions observed.
- Autoscaler did not add workers immediately; we see worker CPU thresholds oscillating but not crossing the autoscale threshold.

I've attached the runbook snippet and a short metrics snapshot. Can we get the priority on mitigation path and a customer message?

Connor
SRE — Redwood Inference

Attachments: greengrid_runbook_v2.pdf, prod-metrics-snapshot-20260612.png

From: connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-12T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] GreenGrid prod latency spike (us-east-1) — mitigation proposal

Short status and proposed mitigation: 
Root cause (prelim): the gptx-13b-q4 variant rollout increased working set for KV caches; combined with a GC-like eviction pattern and a bug in the CPU-based autoscaler threshold, we saw more frequent small batches and queuing. That amplifies tail latency.

Mitigation options: 
1) Immediate rollback of gptx-13b-q4 for GreenGrid's route to previous variant (gptx-13b-fp16). Estimated time: ~25-45 minutes (deploy rollback + warm caches). Risk: brief request routing churn.
2) Apply a temporary KV cache retention increase and forcibly prewarm cache on existing workers. Estimated time: ~20-40 minutes. Lower risk but partial effectiveness if eviction source remains.
3) Emergency scale-up (add 2 workers) and adjust autoscaler thresholds manually. Estimated time: ~10-25 minutes but consumes reserved capacity.

Recommended immediate action: Option 1 (rollback) + Option 3 in parallel if rollback doesn't restore SLA within 30 minutes. I'll start rollback prep now unless we prefer different approach.

I'll also open SUP-7891 and attach metrics slices. Will update in 15 min.

Connor
(Oncall SRE)

From: maya_srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-12T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GreenGrid prod latency spike — rollout context & next steps

Laura / Connor —
This variant rollout was part of a targeted canary for customers on the "performance-opt" track. GreenGrid was in the canary cohort to validate lower-cost quantized variants. It was not a broad rollout.

Action items / asks from Product side: 
- If we rollback, please capture exact metrics and a timestamped snapshot for postmortem and for an eval against our regression test suite.
- If the KV eviction pattern is reproducible, add a regression test that simulates the same batch/sequence distribution.
- We should create a short roadmap ticket to harden autoscaler heuristics (SUP-7891 -> link in Ticket).

I'll prioritize the ticket and can own postmortem coordination. We should also decide whether to offer GreenGrid an SLA credit proactively. 

Maya
Product Manager, Serving Runtime

Date: 2026-06-12T09:55:00-07:00
Subject: Draft: customer notification for GreenGrid (please review)

Tom / GreenGrid ops —

We want to make you aware of a temporary performance degradation affecting inference latency for your production route in us-east-1. Our team detected elevated latency starting at ~08:58 PDT. We are actively mitigating the issue and expect normal performance to resume within the next 60-120 minutes. There is no evidence of data loss or increased error rates.

What we're doing: we are rolling back a recent model variant for your route, prewarming caches, and monitoring traffic. We will follow up with a short incident summary and any impact to SLA.

Estimated ETA: 60–120 minutes.

We appreciate your patience and will keep you updated every 30 minutes or on meaningful changes.

—Sean Gallagher
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Please review and suggest edits. Laura: do you want to add credit/escalation language?

Subject: Re: Draft: customer notification for GreenGrid (please review)

Sean — I like this. Minor edits: tighten ETA to "within 60 minutes" if rollback completes, and add: "If this incident results in a material SLA impact, we will proactively discuss a credit as part of the incident wrap-up."

Hannah — can you send the communication to Tom and ops-contacts once we have confirmation that rollback is started? Please use the attached final draft (customer_comms_draft.txt).

Laura

Cc: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-12T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Update: rollback started — monitoring

Rollback of gptx-13b-q4 for GreenGrid route started at 10:28 PDT. We are seeing cache warm-up and a steady drop in queue length. P95 latency improved ~40% within the first 8 minutes; P99 still elevated but trending down. No errors introduced by the rollback.

If we continue to see improvement over the next 30 minutes, we'll keep the rollback and schedule a controlled re-test once autoscaler heuristics are patched. I'll post a closure update once we confirm stable metrics for 30 minutes.

Connor

Attachments: prod-metrics-snapshot-20260612.png

From: connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, maya_srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, hannah_schnitt@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-13T02:05:00-07:00
Subject: Incident closed — GreenGrid latency restored

Final update: rollback remained in place; P95/P99 returned to baseline by 23:10 UTC (11:10 PDT). We ran a 30-minute stability window and verified autoscaler will not trigger falsely after manual threshold adjustment. Root cause confirmed: interaction between quantized variant memory working set and cache eviction pattern + autoscaler threshold mismatch.

Next steps (assigned):
- SRE (Connor/Hannah): ship autoscaler guard clause and add long-tail workload test (SUP-7891).
- Product (Maya): coordinate postmortem, add regression test to preflight suite.
- CS (Sean): send final incident summary to GreenGrid (use the attached customer_comms_draft.txt as base).
- Ops/Finance (Evelyn): review SLA credit exception if requested.

I'll close the incident ticket and link the postmortem doc in the Drive folder.

Connor
SRE — Redwood Inference
